:::{#exm-error-rate}
#### Test error rate of a low-birth-weight classifier

The `birthwt` data hold births at Baystate Medical Center in Springfield, Massachusetts [@hosmer1989applied],
as distributed in R's `MASS` package [@venables2002modern].
The outcome `low` is 1 for a birth weight under 2.5 kg and 0 otherwise.
We fit a logistic regression of `low` on the mother's age, weight at her last menstrual period, smoking status,
history of hypertension, and presence of uterine irritability.
The fitted model predicts `low = 1` when its fitted probability exceeds 0.5.
We use every third row as the [test set](#def-test-set)
and fit on the remaining rows, the [training set](#def-training-set).

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: error-rate-r
#| code-fold: false
birthwt <- read.csv("data/birthwt.csv")
is_test <- seq_len(nrow(birthwt)) %% 3 == 0

fit_low <- glm(
  low ~ age + lwt + smoke + ht + ui,
  family = binomial,
  data = birthwt[!is_test, ]
)

predicted_low <- function(data) {
  as.integer(predict(fit_low, newdata = data, type = "response") > 0.5)
}

error_rates <- c(
  training = mean(predicted_low(birthwt[!is_test, ]) != birthwt$low[!is_test]),
  test = mean(predicted_low(birthwt[is_test, ]) != birthwt$low[is_test])
)
error_rates
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: error-rate-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

birthwt = pd.read_csv("data/birthwt.csv")
is_test = (np.arange(1, len(birthwt) + 1) % 3 == 0)

fit_low = smf.logit(
    "low ~ age + lwt + smoke + ht + ui", data=birthwt[~is_test]
).fit(disp=False)


def predicted_low(data):
    return (fit_low.predict(data) > 0.5).astype(int)


error_rates = {
    "training": (predicted_low(birthwt[~is_test]) != birthwt["low"][~is_test]).mean(),
    "test": (predicted_low(birthwt[is_test]) != birthwt["low"][is_test]).mean(),
}
error_rates
```

:::

Of the `r nrow(birthwt)` births, `r sum(is_test)` are in the test set.
The fitted model gets the wrong birth-weight category for
`r round(100 * error_rates[["test"]], 1)`% of the test births,
so its test error rate is `r round(error_rates[["test"]], 3)`.
Its training error rate is `r round(error_rates[["training"]], 3)`.

:::
